form_cues: RIGHT arm only; the left arm rests comfortably and never grips, pushes, or braces.
Use only a supported machine approved for independent one-arm operation; ask staff to check setup.
Keep your back against the pad and torso still. Skip if staying stable needs the left arm.
Choose a light comfortable resistance on the actual machine; stop well before straining.
notes: Conditional right-side variation during left-forearm protection, not clearance to load the injured arm. No starting weight is assumed. A suitable machine has not been confirmed at this gym. Prefer a selectorized machine; ask staff to handle adjustments or any plates. Photo and linked demonstration use both arms; do not copy their left-hand position. Do not substitute a Smith machine, dumbbells, or an unsupported cable press.
instructions: Ask staff to confirm that the machine allows independent right-arm pressing and safe entry, setup, release, and exit without using the left hand or elbow. Skip if it requires both handles or left-arm stabilization.

Have the seat and resistance adjusted so the right handle starts near mid-chest and your back is supported. Do not carry, load, or unload plates with the left arm. Use a light comfortable resistance and record the actual weight.
Rest the left arm comfortably in your lap or on a non-moving support, clear of the moving equipment. It stays relaxed throughout; do not hold the unused handle or press into the seat.

With feet planted and torso against the pad, press the right handle forward smoothly through a comfortable range. Avoid twisting, breath-holding, or grinding; keep at least four good repetitions in reserve.

Return the right handle slowly and fully settle the machine before exiting. Stop for any left-forearm symptoms or need to brace with the left arm. Omit the movement next time if symptoms are worse later that day or the next morning.
